At the head that pass was written at, the swept count was 3,739 = main's 3,703 plus that branch's 36, and `surfaces` was 468 = main's 465 plus that change's three directories; both were re-derived with `check-evidence.mjs`'s own walker against that tree rather than carried from either side. THE FIELDS THIS FILE SHIPS READ `frames` 4,051 AND `surfaces` 494, and that is this head's arithmetic rather than that one's: 4,780 committed WebP files, 729 of them inside the 63 declared supplementary sets, and 494 rows in the merged `STORIES` literal (main's 483 plus this branch's eleven `chat-canonical-quote` entries, one of them a second viewport of a story already in the list). Re-derived by script on this head, the way the sentence above describes. `srcTree`/`scriptsTree` are `git rev-parse HEAD:src` / `HEAD:scripts` for the TREE THE EVIDENCE SHIPS IN - the commit that carries this file - which is not necessarily the commit `head` names: `head` names the commit the frames were last TAKEN at, and a later pass that re-stamps without re-taking them reads the tree off its own HEAD. Where the two differ, the re-derivation is recorded in `remediationRecord`. The re-capture that re-derived them is measured in `partialCapture.rebaseMeasurement`: nothing main landed invalidates these frames, and the numbers say what each of the ten frames that moved actually moved by.

TWENTIETH RECORD IN THIS FILE'S SERIES, AND THE FIRST THAT CARRIES FRAMES OF THIS SET RE-TAKEN RATHER THAN RE-DERIVED. The commit it belongs to is round 2's remediation, and the defect it answers was found by four independent streams converging on it (design round 2's D4, review's F1, QA's Q-1, UX's U4): `#218` moved the New chat row's current ground to `rowCurrent = "bg-sunken text-ink hover:bg-sunken"`, which is the caps' OWN fill, so on the one row the chord itself creates the caps and their ground are the same role - 1.00:1, ΔE00 0.00 in all twelve palettes - and the caps read as plain monospace glyphs exactly when the user has just used the chord they name. The glyph ink stays legible there (6.33-12.59:1): this was the affordance, not legibility.

WHAT ANSWERS IT, AND HOW IT IS ASSERTED. A boundary on the caps while that row is current, drawn as an inset outline (`outline-solid outline-1 -outline-offset-1 outline-control`) rather than a border, because a border enters the box model and would move the caps 1px per side in one state only - the same shift this row retires `border-control` on the ROW itself for. `borderControl` on that ground measures 3.13-5.91:1 across the twelve palettes (worst: iceberg 3.13), clearing `docs/branding.md` § 3's 3:1 structural floor in every one; QA's alternative, the cap stepping to `bg-elevated` on a current row, measured 1.20-1.55:1 there and was rejected. The guarantee is ASSERTED: two `STRUCTURAL_CALL_SITES` rows in `scripts/contrast-contract.mjs`, one pinning the condition that puts the edge on the element and one the class it puts there, because no palette assertion can see a class. THE REST STATE IS UNTOUCHED, and that is measured rather than claimed: `after-sidebar-dark.png`, `after-sidebar-light.png` and `after-row-dark.png` re-captured through the same harness at the same viewport return `magick compare -metric AE` 0, at the same byte sizes as the committed files (76,991 / 76,734 / 8,656).

The row frame differs from the frame it replaces by 30,724 of 128,000 pixels, in ONE 111x43 box - the caps' own box, the same box the sidebar pair differs in one row higher, at +425+1058 - which is the layout-neutrality claim in pixels: an inset outline cannot move the row, and the frame says it did not. It wrote the six frames of `chat-run-panel/{back-to-roster,back-pop,close-from-reader}` at the two brand themes, and the SIX BEFORE halves of the same three stories live in the declared supplementary set `run-panel-back-before/`, captured from the same tree with `origin/main`'s component swapped in. Earlier wording here said the key existed so main's `addedAtHead`/`refreshedAtHead` would keep naming main's passes; that is no longer true of this pass, because re-capturing the frames MOVED both onto `dd5f20e0d` - and reachability is read from exactly those two fields, so they say what they are. imageExpandPass.measured: Off the committed frames, by thresholding the picture's light ground and trimming to it: `expanded` is 1152x432 at +64,+234 in a 1280x900 frame (the 90vw cap binding, 64px on each side = the 5% margin), and `expanded-small-image` is 240x180 at +200,+120 in a 640x420 frame - the picture's own size, in a box of 576x378 it never used.

imageExpandPass.notCovered: A real-engine pointer press aimed at a POINT outside the picture. The `browser` tool clicks an element by selector and cannot aim at a coordinate, and this surface's centre IS the picture; the scrim press is evidenced by the element the press lands on (jsdom) plus the measured geometry that makes that element genuinely outside the layer. A coordinate-capable harness closes it - QA's place, named in the set's README rather than implied away.

supplementary.source: scripts/capture-evidence.mjs against unmodified origin/main at 54bf411e0 (chore(release): bump version to 0.19.0), same story file, same fixtures and same viewports as chat-ask-options/, with only what main's tree cannot compile removed: the onAnswer and answering props, and the recommended fixture key, which is not on main's PendingDesktopGate
why: The fixed frames cannot show what was wrong, because the defect is an ABSENCE: nothing on the ask card was pressable, and an absence does not photograph. This set is main's own card under the same fixtures - inert muted text, label and consequence run together on one line, no recommended marker, and 'Type your answer below.' as the only affordance - so the reviewer can see what changed instead of taking it on trust.

It cannot be regenerated by a sweep: a sweep captures the CURRENT tree, while these need main's own CanonicalTranscript under the same story. Declared as its own set so clearSweptFrames preserves it and the sweep's own count stays honest.

Two of the eight surfaces are meant to look IDENTICAL to their chat-ask-options/ twins - secret-ask (a secret ask arrives with empty options) and approval-unchanged (approvals carry no options and are out of scope). The pair is what proves the non-goals were not disturbed, which no frame of the new card alone can show.

THE BASE THIS SET WAS TAKEN FROM IS NOT THE BRANCH'S REBASE TARGET, and an earlier version of this sentence said it was. Corrected: 54bf411e0 is `chore(release): bump version to 0.19.0` and sits BEHIND the commit this branch was cut from, f3eb589c1 (`0.19.1`). The earlier narration also ordered the rebases backwards -- it had the branch rebased onto 54bf411e0 and then 'again' onto 79d0dc889 (#120) -- which cannot have happened: 79d0dc889 was authored at 22:09 and merged into main after 54bf411e0's 19:16, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 79d0dc889 54bf411e0` is false. What makes the comparison valid is measured rather than narrated, and the measurement is NOT that the diff is empty - an earlier correction of this same sentence said it was, and that was wrong when it was written: `git diff --name-only 54bf411e0..$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)` over `src/renderer/src/features/chat/canonical/**`, `src/renderer/src/features/chat/components/trace/**` and `src/renderer/src/features/chat/components/message-item/**` returns ELEVEN files at the current base: main's trace tier, main's mentioned-file rebuild, and main's own `reconnect-gap.stories.tsx`. previousPartialCapture.provenanceNote:
THE REBASE, and the first one here that re-stamps without re-capturing. `main` moved three times under this branch during the round - to `e4d074c60` (0.19.6), to `98c32e85e` (0.19.7 plus #138, which the previous pass re-captured at), and then to `c0570ea60` (0.19.7 plus #136). That move is not packaging: it adds `src/renderer/src/features/chat/clear-search.ts` and rewrites the search field in `src/renderer/src/features/chat/components/chat-sidebar.tsx` (+51/-8), so `srcTree` moved for the first time in any of these rebases, and `scripts/` moved with it (`scripts/clear-search.test.mjs`). A stamp whose tree has moved is exactly the case the earlier passes answered by re-capturing; this one answered it with two facts about the frames. The first is the shape of the change: it paints a clear control INSIDE the field and only while the query is non-empty (the `{query && ...}` guard around the button in `chat-sidebar.tsx`), plus a `pr-9` on the input that reserves the control's column and a `my-2` moved from the input onto a `relative` wrapper around it, which reproduces the same box - so with an empty query the field renders the same placeholder, the same border and the same box as it did before. The second is the measurement that closes it: `clear-search/before-rest` and `clear-search/after-rest` are BYTE-IDENTICAL in both themes, the same empty-query sidebar painted once on the pre-change tree and once on the post-change tree, so nothing in that state depends on #136 at all. Every frame in this tree of that state is therefore unchanged, and the only frames whose state differs are the non-empty-query ones, all of them in `clear-search` itself, which were taken on the changed tree by #136. The sets that carry the field besides `clear-search` were looked at rather than assumed to be empty: `chat-title` and `sidebar-new-chat` draw the empty placeholder with no clear control in all 38 of their frames across both themes, `model-picker-feedback` shows the same empty field behind its scrim, and `mentioned-files-app` is cropped to the canvas panel's own measured rect and carries no sidebar at all; no other set in the tree is about that field - `clear-search`'s own README and readbacks are the only evidence in the tree that names it. Nothing else in the tree was a different source for these pixels either, and that is measurable in the same way: 0 `.webp` differ between the head the previous pass ran at (`98b827108`, orphaned by the force-push that carried this re-stamp) and this head.

THE SYNC MERGE, and what it does and does not claim about the frames. `main` moved three times more - to `6f9bc2d04` (#140: the desktop toolchain, Electron 44 and TypeScript 7), to `4ffc3f2b5` (#139: the New chat row aligned with All chats, without the pill) and to `ad09ec6b4` (the 0.20.1 release) - and this branch was merged up onto it rather than replayed onto it, because a rebase would rewrite all twenty-two commits and orphan every citation this manifest carries while changing no pixel a reader can see. Two paths conflicted: `package.json` (resolved the same way as before - `main`'s `version` line, now 0.20.1, with the UNION of the two sides' `test:desktop` lists, which now carry all three of the test files the sides added, this branch's `mentioned-files.test.mjs` and `main`'s `new-chat-row.test.mjs` and `new-chat-row-evidence.test.mjs`) and this manifest's stamp block, where two re-stamps had to be reconciled; `src/main/index.ts` was auto-merged, both sides' hunks kept. No frame was re-taken for the merge, and the two upstream changes are treated differently for a reason. #140 moves the toolchain (`package.json`, `electron.vite.config.js`, the `tsconfig`s, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, three `scripts/` files, five `src/main/` modules and one renderer component) and not the canvas, the mentioned-files producer or the sidebar, and `main` itself did not re-sweep for it: it re-stamped its trees and committed the toolchain set's own packaged frame beside the swept ones, which is the same position this branch takes for the frames it contributed. #139 does move the sidebar's New chat row, and the three sets that photograph the sidebar (`chat-title`, `sidebar-new-chat` and `model-picker-feedback`'s scrimmed background) predate it: they are pictures of the sidebar as it stood at the heads their `capturedAtHead` fields name, this manifest makes no claim that they show the post-#139 row, and `main` carries that change's own before/after evidence beside them in the `new-chat-row` set - which is why the merge adds that set rather than re-driving those older frames. Nothing on either side of the merge touches this branch's own contribution: the canvas surfaces and `mentioned-files-app` are cropped to panels that #139 and #140 do not paint.

unchangedControl.why: The honesty check for this pass, and the reason a moved frame is legible as one: a surface this rebase does not paint differently was re-captured through the same command, on the same host, in the same session as the nine it does. All twelve came back BYTE-IDENTICAL, so the encoder and the renderer are deterministic here at this load. The class the moved frames belong to was measured the same way in the previous pass, which ran `audio-viewer` twice: its `neon` frame - which moved in the first run of BOTH passes - came back exactly the committed bytes in that second run. Neither control separates the widget from the encoder for `pdf-viewer/localOperatorDark`, whose difference is the platform PDF plugin not painting at all and which reproduced byte-for-byte instead (see `recaptureNote`).

previousPartialCapture.recaptureNote: Re-captured in place, at the rebased head, and the result is one-sided: 101 of the 108 frames came back BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed bytes, and all 48 of the four Files surfaces plus all 12 control frames are among them. The 7 that moved are media-viewer frames - pdf 1 (`localOperatorDark`), image 2 (`synth`, `radient`), audio 2 (`neon`, `radient`), video 2 (`synth`, `radient`) - and six of the seven moved only at the lossy encoder's own quantisation scale: at an 8% tolerance (20/255) ZERO pixels differ, and the worst RMSE is 0.00054 (`video-viewer/radient`, 4,342 px of 1,152,000). That class is established rather than assumed: the same command on the same tree was run twice in the previous pass, and `audio-viewer/neon` - which moved in both passes' first runs - came back EXACTLY the committed bytes in one of them, so the movement is the widget repaint and the encoder and a frame that has moved is not read as a change unless it survives a second run. The seventh, `pdf-viewer/localOperatorDark`, is a reproducible platform paint failure and not that class: this session's private headless Chrome never painted the PDF guest document - a probe at 640,200 reads the platform field `srgb(40,40,40)` where the committed frame reads the white page - with a byte-for-byte identical difference (204,364 px, 163,673 of them above 8%) in both passes. The viewer's own source (`pdf-preview.tsx`, `canvas-file-viewer.tsx`, the story) is untouched by `main`'s move, and this branch's canvas hunks in `chat-page.tsx` and `chat-content.tsx` - the one host surface the rebase had to carry - survive line-for-line, so the committed frame is the one that depicts the surface under review; it is retained and NO byte-identity claim is made for it. The 7 frames whose committed bytes are retained are the same picture the re-capture measured.

captureOrigin.note: Two preserved records, not one, and the fields are not interchangeable. `head`/`capturedAt` name the commit and the time the capture was taken at. `srcTree`/`scriptsTree` are the tree hashes the aggregate fields carried before they were re-derived, and they never described `head`'s trees: they are `8d019993e`'s (`git rev-parse 8d019993e:src` = 6253e4196..., `:scripts` = 2fe452ad2...), the upstream commit whose stamp block wrote them, while `0f19ae5e2:src` is 5e6095c258e8.... `dirtyWorkingTree` is the branch's own `8e8660808`-era pass recording the scratch `.storybook/main.ts` docgen override that capture needed, deliberately not a current value: a re-derivation does not make an older capture clean. No frame was recaptured for this re-derivation, and these frames are not claimed to be current. What covers this branch's delta is specific: the five in `job-result-label-round5` show the job-result and statement register this branch owns, and the six under `chat-canonical-notices/session-incidents`, `session-incidents-narrow` and `notice-lengths` show the incident and notice registers - all historical captures, none of them a frame at this head, and one row of `session-incidents` and `session-incidents-narrow` paints through upstream's receipt model there instead. The rest of this branch's delta - the tooltip/selection union in `disclosure.tsx` and the scripts the gate reads - has no frame at this head, so its evidence is the PR's test and rebase rounds rather than a picture.

commandPaletteCapture.reshoot: FOUR sweeps on this branch, because each answered a review finding that changed what the frames show: the first for the feature itself, then the design round's D1/D3/D5/D6, then D7 (the fold out of the flow) and U7 (the scrim clearing the connection banner), and last the fold GATE itself — the fade's condition was the result cap in one cut and an effect-keyed measurement in the next, neither of which rendered, because Radix defers its portal by one commit and the effects ran before the list existed. A callback ref fixed the timing and the fade is in the frames now (15708 pixels differ from the previous cut of the same predicate, against 15 for the version that measured nothing).
commandPaletteCapture.stamps: `head`, `capturedAt`, `srcTree` and `scriptsTree` describe the tree the frames SHIP IN, which is why they are re-derived after each merge of `main` rather than left at the capture's own commit; `captureOrigin` keeps the older capture's own pair, which no gate reads. `partialCapture` is `main`'s record with this branch's pass accumulated into it, per the field's own definition.
commandPaletteCapture.offlineNote: Both captures are the OFFLINE palette, and that is the state rather than a limitation worked around: the harness refuses to sweep while a Local Operator backend answers on the configured port, because a frame showing the operator's own agents and settings is not a function of the tree. The worktree's `.env` was pointed at a dead port for each sweep and restored afterwards.
commandPaletteCapture.notInTheseFrames: Conversations, the settings registry rows and the palette's four panel ROWS need a live backend and a pane behind it, so neither capture contains them. The panels THEMSELVES are captured as their own story sets (`panels-info--*`, `panels-analytics--*`, `panels-session--*`, `chat-usage--*`), named in `docs/evidence/command-palette/README.md`; the row that leads to one is covered by the unit tests and by the QA round.
commandPaletteCapture.checkEvidence: DEFERRED on this machine: another session has held the machine lease `/tmp/local-operator-ui-check-evidence.lock` since 15:27, so this pass is recorded and not certified. `scripts/evidence-manifest.test.mjs` binds the stamps and the aggregates against the tree.
commandPaletteCapture.restampNote: RE-STAMPED, not re-shot: the four fixes after the code review's third round are a condition on a note (`!chats.pending`, which cannot change what an offline frame renders — the capability read has settled by then), a keyboard guard, an unused ref and a test assertion. None of them can move a pixel, so the frames keep their capture head and only the tree stamps move.

keycapsCapture.blocked: The settings rail's current row is the one changed surface with no frame, and the blockage is measured rather than assumed: `shell-app-shell--settings-appearance` sets `documentElement.dataset.capturePending` and clears it only when the settings page renders the Appearance switch, which the offline settings page never does, so the sweep reports `{"drawn":false,"counted":88,"pending":true}` after its 60s bound; the sweep aborts there, before `shell-app-shell--settings` in the same list. Re-shooting that set was also measured and REJECTED: with no backend those stories render the disconnected state where the committed frames show populated panels, so a re-sweep would have replaced better frames with worse ones.
